description: Cross-synthesis (formerly SPECVOCO): extracts the evolving spectral envelope (formants) of input 2 and imposes it on the spectrum of input 1 - input 1 supplies the material, input 2 the timbral shape. Output duration follows the SHORTER input (verified both orders: 2 s x 1 s and 1 s x 2 s both give the 1 s input's analysed duration). CDP requires exactly one of the two extraction flags -f/-p; this entry pins the pitchwise form and always emits -p<fbands> (SoundThread's choice, default 8); the linear-frequencywise -f form is mutually exclusive with -p (passing both refuses with 'Unknown flag -p on command line.') and is reachable via execute(). Deterministic: two runs 1.1 s apart have identical analysis data (only the RIFF LIST date-comment chunk differs). Amplitude follows the donor's envelope too - a flat tone vocoded by a pulsed donor synthesized to an RMS trajectory correlating with the donor at r = 0.89.
musical_use: The classic 'make the water shout' process: vocal or speech-like donors stamp their formant motion onto any sustained, spectrally rich target. Input 1 wants dense, broadband material (noise, textures, sustained chords - things with energy to carve); input 2 wants strong, moving spectral shapes (speech, shouts, animal calls). fbands is the resolution knob: low values (2-4 bands/octave) give a coarse, dark shadow of the donor; 8-12 approach intelligibility. Pitchwise extraction favours low/mid-register donors (the manual recommends frequencywise for material concentrated high - use execute() with -f there). Use -l to strip rumble the donor pushes into the target and -g around 0.5 to tame level buildup (values > 1 amplify, max 10). Chain the output straight into another spectral entry or let auto-PVOC synth it back.

fbands.description: Pitchwise formant extraction: N equally-spaced pitch-bands per octave. CDP's real maximum is analysis-dependent ('Too many formant_bands requested: max for this file is 12' at 44.1 kHz / 1024-point analysis); fractional values accepted (2.5 verified); 0 is accepted by CDP but curated out (min 1). Always emitted (CDP requires -f or -p; entry pins -p). Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read count of formant_bands.').

lof.description: Low frequency below which the spectrum is filtered out (CDP-enforced 5 to 22050: '-l-1' refused with 'Parameter[1] Value (-1.000000) out of range (5.000000 to 22050.000000)'). No cross-check against hif: lof > hif is accepted silently. Breakpoint refused ('brkpnt_files not permitted', parameter 1).

hif.description: High frequency above which the spectrum is filtered out (CDP-enforced 5 to 22050). hif < lof is accepted without warning - keep hif above lof yourself. Breakpoint refused.

gain.description: Amplitude adjustment of the signal, 'normally < 1.0' (banner). CDP-enforced range 0.000002 to 10 ('-g-1' refused quoting '(0.000002 to 10.000000)'; afta8's 0-1 is an advisory subset). Breakpoint refused ('brkpnt_files not permitted', parameter 3).

examples.description: Speech-shaped noise: voice donor carves a noise texture.
examples.expected_use: inputs = [noise/texture, speech]; output .ana lasts as long as the shorter input.

examples.description: Coarse timbral shadowing with rumble removed.
examples.expected_use: Dark, gestural version of the donor's motion on the target's material.

known_issues: CDP requires exactly one of -f / -p; this entry always emits -p via the fbands default. Passing both forms refuses ('Unknown flag -p on command line.'), and the -f (frequencywise) variant is not exposed - use execute() for it. -f0 crashes with 'ERROR: INTERNAL ERROR: (Bug?) / ERROR: Formant array too small: set_specenv_frqs()'.

Output duration = the shorter input's analysed duration (expr indur_min; the .ana analysis grid adds about +1.5% over the source wav duration - 2 s wavs give a 2.029 s .ana - within the duration-model tolerance).
fbands' maximum is analysis-dependent (12 for a 44.1 kHz / default-analysis file; the refusal is 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Too many formant_bands requested: max for this file is 12').
lof/hif are not cross-checked (lof 400 with hif 100 ran silently); no parameter accepts breakpoint files.
Byte-level comparison of two runs differs only in the RIFF LIST chunk (CDP writes a date comment) - compare the data chunk, not raw bytes, when hashing .ana outputs.
Inputs are .ana analysis files; time-domain .wav inputs are auto-converted by the engine's PVOC insertion.
